derivation_notes: The parent law assumes intervention escalation depends only on relative exceedance above the trigger. Here the active-regime unsuppressed residue is additionally damped by exp(-p/p_trigger), so for the same relative exceedance the program suppresses contacts more strongly when the absolute prevalence burden is larger.
change_summary: Relaxed the equal-relative-exceedance assumption by introducing absolute-prevalence modulation into the triggered suppression law. This bends the activation surface in the (p, p_trigger) plane without adding new inputs or states.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Equal relative exceedance above different triggers produces the same controlled-contact fraction, independent of the absolute prevalence scale.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Public and programmatic response can be more decisive when absolute prevalence is plainly high, because case visibility, institutional pressure, and individual risk perception depend on absolute burden as well as whether a nominal trigger has been crossed.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The successor reduces to the parent in the weak absolute-burden modulation limit exp(-p/p_trigger) -> 1, equivalently when the additional absolute-prevalence dependence vanishes.

response_change.parent_relation: For fixed c0 and rho, suppression is controlled only by the normalized excess prevalence (p-p_trigger)/p_trigger through a single activation threshold and one active-regime shape, so the prevalence level at which substantial suppression appears scales linearly with p_trigger.
response_change.child_relation: Keep prevalence-triggered activation but relax the assumption that response depends only on relative exceedance; make suppression depend on both relative exceedance and absolute prevalence so that the effective activation band bends with p_trigger.
response_change.observable_effect: Holding p fixed and rho,c0 fixed, increasing p_trigger can weaken control more strongly at low absolute prevalence than the parent predicts, while at higher absolute prevalence the onset remains comparatively sharper; equivalently, two scenarios with the same p/p_trigger ratio but different absolute p need not have the same c_eff/c0.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when comparing policies with different admissible p_trigger values and prevalence spanning from low to moderate absolute levels near and above the trigger; especially when p_trigger is small enough that the same relative exceedance can occur at materially different absolute p.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, near-trigger cases already show smoothed activation; in holdout, comparing equal p/p_trigger across wider absolute prevalence values reveals that the activation sharpness and effective suppression are not identical once absolute prevalence differs.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when any absolute-prevalence modulation vanishes, so suppression depends only on (p-p_trigger)/p_trigger.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: Absolute prevalence modulates the strength of a prevalence-triggered intervention response.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Public and programmatic response can be more decisive when absolute prevalence is plainly high, because case visibility, institutional pressure, and individual risk perception depend on absolute burden as well as whether a nominal trigger has been crossed.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the mapping no longer collapses to a single relative-exceedance coordinate; the extra saturation factor changes the geometry of equal-response contours in the observed input plane.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Intervention escalation depends only on normalized exceedance above the trigger.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Intervention escalation remains trigger-based but is additionally modulated by absolute prevalence through a saturating burden-sensitive factor.
evolution_contract.before_fragment: c0*(1 - rho*(1 - exp(-(p - p_trigger)/p_trigger - ((p - p_trigger)/p_trigger)**3))*(1 + tanh((p - p_trigger)/p_trigger))/2)
evolution_contract.after_fragment: c0*(1 - rho*(1 - exp(-p/p_trigger)*exp(-(p - p_trigger)/p_trigger - ((p - p_trigger)/p_trigger)**3))*(1 + tanh((p - p_trigger)/p_trigger))/2)
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered when exp(-p/p_trigger) is effectively 1, i.e. when the added absolute-prevalence modulation is removed.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Compare cases with equal p/p_trigger but different absolute p, while holding c0 and rho fixed: the parent predicts identical suppression because it depends only on (p-p_trigger)/p_trigger, whereas the child predicts lower c_eff at larger absolute p through the extra exp(-p/p_trigger) damping of the active-regime residue.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because its target mapping is exactly a one-dimensional function of the relative-excess coordinate once c0 and rho are fixed. Refitting rho or reshaping the existing threshold terms only changes that shared one-dimensional curve; it cannot assign different c_eff values to two observations that share the same p/p_trigger but differ in absolute p.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when comparing policies with different admissible p_trigger values and prevalence spanning from low to moderate absolute levels near and above the trigger; especially when p_trigger is small enough that the same relative exceedance can occur at materially different absolute p.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, near-trigger cases already show smoothed activation; in holdout, comparing equal p/p_trigger across wider absolute prevalence values reveals that the activation sharpness and effective suppression are not identical once absolute prevalence differs.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when any absolute-prevalence modulation vanishes, so suppression depends only on (p-p_trigger)/p_trigger.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current law treats intervention activation and escalation as depending only on prevalence relative to the trigger, ignoring that operational urgency and adherence can also depend on the absolute prevalence level even at the same relative exceedance.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Equal relative exceedance above different triggers produces the same controlled-contact fraction, independent of the absolute prevalence scale.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Public and programmatic response can be more decisive when absolute prevalence is plainly high, because case visibility, institutional pressure, and individual risk perception depend on absolute burden as well as whether a nominal trigger has been crossed.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response: for fixed c0 and rho, c_eff/c0 is effectively a one-dimensional function of (p-p_trigger)/p_trigger, so any two conditions with the same p/p_trigger receive the same suppression. Child refinement: preserve the same prevalence-triggered control concept but allow the onset/strength map to depend additionally on absolute prevalence, changing the threshold geometry in the (p,p_trigger) plane rather than merely rescaling coefficients. Concrete distinguishing condition: vary p_trigger across admissible policy values while holding p and rho fixed, or compare pairs with equal p/p_trigger but different absolute p; then the child allows different c_eff values whereas the parent with one shared parameter set cannot, because its mapping collapses these cases onto the same relative-excess coordinate. This is a changed target mapping, not just auxiliary dynamics, since c_eff itself changes as a function of supplied inputs. The effect is scientifically admissible when prevalence is low-to-moderate and surveillance/behavior respond differently to absolute burden; limitation: if the sampled domain keeps absolute prevalence tightly tied to p_trigger so that equal relative exceedance never occurs at meaningfully different p, the contrast will be weak.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Use a finite-capacity, saturation, threshold, or regime-transition response.

scenario_text: Determine the effective contact rate used by an epidemic-control program that activates when measured prevalence reaches a specified trigger. Below the trigger, contacts remain at their baseline level; at or above it, a fixed fraction of contacts is suppressed. Prevalence, the uncontrolled contact rate, the trigger, and intervention strength are independently sampled policy conditions. The target is the immediate controlled contact rate, without modeling delayed behavioral adjustment.
